title: Discovering Kepler-90i: A Human-Missed Planet
text: Nobody ever had time to check? In 2017, Google engineer Christopher Shallue and astronomer Andrew Vanderburg tried something different. They trained a neural network on 15,000 light curves humans had already labeled by hand. The network didn't look at one curve, it compared two views. The full orbit and a close-up of just the dip. title: Conclusion: AI as a Tool for Prioritizing Human Time
text: Eight planets outside our own. Overall, the network told real planets from false alarms correctly 96% of the time. This same idea now runs continuously. Vera Rubin Observatory alone produces about 10 terabytes of images every night. That's up to 7 million alerts a night across a 10-year survey expected to total roughly 60 petabytes. No human team could review that. The universe was never short on signals, just on hours. AI doesn't replace the astronomer looking through the telescope. It decides what's worth their time.
